dossiers.thesis_summary: FDA decision on the mitapivat sickle cell sNDA (accelerated approval pathway, Priority Review) is real, unfired and idiosyncratic, but the goal date moved from 2026-11-01 to 2027-02-01 after FDA classed Agios' REMS-related response as a major amendment (company PR 2026-10-30, reaffirmed in Q3 release 2026-11-05). Company says it is in labeling discussions including elements of a potential REMS, and reports no sickle cell liver-injury cases of the thalassemia pattern in ~9 months of extra open-label safety data. On re-derived levels ($38 approval / $24 rejection) the $31.18 price already implies ~51% approval odds; at my 60% the probability-weighted value is $32.40, only ~+4% above price.
dossiers.kill_risk: Most load-bearing claim: "labeling discussions mean the review is on an approvable track and the extension is about REMS, not efficacy." Residual risk I could not refute: (1) that framing is the company's own; no FDA document is public, and RISE UP missed the pain-crisis endpoint (2.6 vs 3.1 annualized, p=0.12), so the file rests on hemoglobin response under accelerated approval with the voxelotor withdrawal as the class precedent - a CRL or a second extension is still credible. (2) Even on approval, a restrictive REMS (the existing AQVESME one requires liver tests every 4 weeks for 24 weeks plus prescriber/pharmacy certification) into a 25,000-patient community setting would cap the win leg below $38. (3) An effective automatic shelf (S-3ASR, Feb-2026, per skeptic record; not re-verified by me) lets the company sell stock into an approval pop. (4) The price is only ~51% of the way from floor to target, so the payoff is close to symmetric - the event is live but the spread is thin.
discrepancies: dated_milestone: board 2026-11-01 -> live 2027-02-01 - FDA extended the PDUFA goal date three months (major amendment on REMS information request), Agios PR 2026-10-30 and Q3 release 2026-11-05; the board date has already passed without a decision

fair_value_target: board 44 -> live 38 - board number dates from 2026-08-04, before the tebapivat setback and the delay; I cannot reproduce 44. Re-derived as rejection-case value 24 + sickle cell layer ~14/sh (~$840M), with no re-rating of the existing franchise or pipeline on an SCD approval
downside_floor: board 23 -> live 24 - rebuilt from Q3 numbers: cash $907M / ~59.7M shares = $15.2/sh plus existing mitapivat franchise at ~2.4x the $222M annualized Q3 run-rate = ~$8.9/sh
win_prob: board null -> live 0.60 - my estimate; market-implied is ~0.51 at $31.18 on the 38/24 levels
live_price: board 30.54 -> live 31.18 (FMP quote, 2026-11-10; previous close 31.38)
dossiers.dossier_note:
STATUS: PENDING_HARD on the new date. The timeline SLIPPED once, from 2026-11-01 to 2027-02-01 (PDUFA goal date; FDA asked for information on whether a REMS is needed for sickle cell, Agios answered with ~9 months of extra RISE UP open-label safety data, FDA classed it a major amendment = standard 3-month extension). I emit PENDING_HARD rather than SLIPPED because the new date is a formal FDA goal date and the weekly debate already carries it; the CRO should still treat this as a once-slipped clock. Stock fell >15% on 2026-10-30. No advisory committee disclosed. Days to milestone from today: 83.

LIVE FACTS (Q3 release + call, 2026-11-05; 10-Q filed same day): mitapivat net revenue $55.4M (US $48.7M, +20% q/q; ex-US $6.6M) vs $12.9M a year ago; AQVESME 619 cumulative completed start forms (177 in Q3), ~75% persistence at ~6 months; cash and securities $907.0M; Q3 net loss $65M; non-GAAP profitability targeted for 2028 assuming a 2027 SCD launch; initial SCD target ~25,000 treated US patients; field teams hired. CMO said REMS could range from education to more extensive restrictions and would not say which is under discussion. More RISE UP data at ASH in December (open-label: 62.7% hemoglobin responders) - a soft data point before the decision, not the resolving event.

ARITHMETIC. Shares ~59.7M (market cap $1,861.8M / $31.18; skeptic record cites 59,780,890 from the 10-Q). Enterprise value = 1,862 - 907 = ~$955M.
Rejection leg $24: cash $15.2/sh + existing franchise $8.9/sh (2.4x $222M run-rate = $532M). No credit for pipeline (AG-236 Ph2/3 start by year-end, cevidoplenib Ph3 1H-2028), which roughly offsets ~2 years of burn to the 2028 profitability target. This is above the 52-week low of $22.24, so a rejection could overshoot the floor by ~7%; and note the 5-Nov close of $28.27 was a price WITH the option alive, not a floor.
Approval leg $38: $24 + ~$14/sh for sickle cell (~$840M, roughly 1.7x a ~$500M peak-sales case = 25,000 patients x ~8% share x ~$250k net; these penetration and net-price inputs are my assumptions, not company guidance). I agree with the skeptic that an SCD approval does not justify a higher multiple on the thalassemia/PK revenue or the pipeline, so none is included.
Result: upside +21.9% / downside -23.0% from $31.18 = ~0.95:1. Market-implied approval probability = (31.18-24)/(38-24) = 51%. At my 60%: 0.6x38 + 0.4x24 = $32.40, +3.9% vs price. Win_prob 0.60 reasoning: labeling/REMS discussions under way and clean incremental liver-safety data argue above a coin flip; the missed pain endpoint, accelerated-approval reliance on hemoglobin and the voxelotor precedent hold it well below typical late-review approval rates.

TAKEOUT LENS: no lift applied. The asset is commercial-stage in rare hematology and would be a logical fit for a large hematology franchise, but I found no recent named comparable deal in the live record to anchor a premium, and the one well-known sickle cell comp (Pfizer/Global Blood Therapeutics, $5.4B, Aug-2022) ended in the voxelotor withdrawal - it cuts against paying up before the label and REMS are known. Takeout stays undated optionality, not part of the target.

NOT VERIFIED: GlobeNewswire pages returned 403, so the two company releases were read from the FMP press-release feed text and a MarketBeat call summary, not the full documents; the S-3ASR shelf and the REIGNITE/nephropathy-trial registry points come from the skeptic record and were not re-checked.

dossiers.thesis_summary: Savara's MOLBREEVI (molgramostim inhalation) application in autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis has an FDA target action date of 22 November 2026 (a Sunday; action likely by Fri 20 Nov or announced Mon 23 Nov), under priority review with Breakthrough designation and no advisory committee. The date is restated in the 10-Q filed 9 November 2026 with a clean subsequent-events note, and no 8-K or press release since. The event is real, dated, unfired and idiosyncratic. The numbers are weaker than the board's: on the 10-Q's fully diluted approval-branch share count (278.2m) the win price is about $7.00, not $9; a rejection floor is about $1.25, not $2.25. At a 75% approval probability the expected value is about $5.56 against a live $4.86 (+14%), with break-even probability about 63%.
dossiers.kill_risk: Manufacturing/inspection status is undisclosed 12 days out. This exact file was refused in May 2025 on its manufacturing section, and the April 2026 three-month extension came from a 'major amendment' whose content Savara never specified; the word 'inspection' does not appear in the 9 Nov 10-Q. A manufacturing-driven complete response letter is the credible loss path and would also forfeit about $150m of approval-gated capital (RTW $75m royalty, Hercules up to $75m) with only $129.6m cash and roughly $35-43m quarterly burn, forcing a dilutive raise. Secondary: FDA can miss the date without notice, and at $4.86 the EV edge (+14%) is thin enough that a modestly lower approval probability (below ~63%) makes it negative.
discrepancies: fair_value_target: board 9 -> live 7.00 — board $9 is not reproducible; the debate's own $1.87bn approval value, less the PARI 3.5% net-sales royalty (10-Q Note 9, ~$57m) and with the RTW royalty capped at its $187.5m Maximum Payment (PV ~$120m vs $230m deducted), divided by the 10-Q approval-branch diluted count of 278.2m shares, gives about $7.0

downside_floor: board 2.25 -> live 1.25 — $2.25 (-54%) is too shallow for a second regulatory failure with $129.6m cash, $30.2m debt, and $150m of approval-gated capital forfeited; hard net backing is only ~$0.3/share, floor rests on residual asset value of ~$200-250m

dossiers.thesis_summary: Annexon's independent data monitoring committee will assess the Month 15 primary endpoint of the single Phase 3 ARCHER II trial of vonaprument in geographic atrophy in Q4 2026. The company restated "on track for Q4 2026" in its 9 November 2026 results release, and nothing has fired: the only filings since are the 10-Q and results 8-K of 9 November, and the newswire has nothing after that date. The outcome is binary inside the window: either the committee says the endpoint is met (sub-study results follow in Q1 2027), or it recommends continuing to the Month 24 endpoint. A "met" verdict pays about $9.50 in the window, not the board's $11; the lose leg is a "continue to Month 24" message at about $1.60. At $4.26 the price implies roughly a 34% chance of a win, so the edge is thin and rests entirely on the win probability being above that.
dossiers.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the win probability (my 40%) exceeds the roughly 34% the price implies; I could not confirm it from the live record, and several facts cut against it. The Phase 2 vision signal was a secondary endpoint in a trial that missed its lesion-growth primary. In August 2026 the company added a Month 24 dual primary endpoint, which splits the statistical alpha and reads as a hedge on Month 15. The "lose" outcome is a quiet "continue to Month 24" recommendation with the company still masked, so no data will be available to argue with. At 34% or lower the trade has zero or negative expected value. Two further risks: the Q4 date is company guidance only (the registry does not date Month 15), so a slip into Q1 2027 would strand dated option structures; and the company has been issuing shares into the run-up (about 671,000 shares added between 30 September and 5 November) with at-the-market capacity still open, so a "met" print is likely to be sold into or followed by a raise, capping the win leg.

dossiers.dossier_note:
STATUS: PENDING_HARD, unfired as of 10 November 2026. The 9 November results release (GlobeNewswire) says the Month 15 primary endpoint assessment is "on track for Q4 2026". SEC filings since 1 September are a Form 4 (25 September), a 13G/A (5 November), and the 8-K and 10-Q (both 9 November); there is no data 8-K. The guidance has been restated on 12 August, 24 September, 28 October, at the 3 November investor event and on 9 November. I could not open the 9 November release itself (HTTP 403), so the "met versus continue to Month 24" wording comes from the board's quote and matches the Q2 release.

MILESTONE: kept at 2026-12-31 as the outer bound of the guided quarter. This is company guidance, not a regulator date. Staging stays false.

EVENT STRUCTURE: there are two outcomes in the window. Either the committee recommends that the endpoint is met, with the two sub-studies read in Q1 2027, or it recommends continuing to the Month 24 dual primary endpoint (added 12 August 2026; trial completion Q3 2027). There is no explicit futility arm, so the lose leg is a "continue" message, not a trial failure.

CAPITAL STRUCTURE (10-Q, 9 November 2026):
- Shares: 190,763,984 common at 5 November, plus 14,745,093 pre-funded warrants, for 205.5M.
- Cash and short-term investments: $213.4M at 30 September. Oxford term loan: $49.3M. Net cash is about $164M, or $0.80 per share.
- Runway: into 2028.
- Issuance: 12,269,877 shares for $66.2M net in the first nine months of 2026, and the count rose about 671,000 between 30 September and 5 November. My extract did not attribute these to the at-the-market programme or state remaining capacity; the skeptic's $115.2M figure is unverified by me, but the share-count rise is consistent with it.

WIN LEG, $9.50 (board $11 corrected): 9.5 x 205.5M = $1.95B market cap, about $1.8B enterprise value. That is roughly 30% of the two approved-asset comps in this indication. A masked "met" verdict with no numbers, sub-studies pending and a single study does not justify more inside the window. Street targets ($11-16; MarketBeat consensus $15.33 in August) are stale 12-month figures that embed the Q1 2027 data.

LOSE LEG, $1.60 (kept): net cash $0.80 per share today, about $0.68 by year-end on burn, plus roughly $0.75-1.00 for the tanruprubart Guillain-Barre programme (US filing guided for Q4 2026, EU application under review) and the remaining Month 24 option. The 52-week low of $2.54 was set with the trial option intact. With the biotech index at a five-year high, the floor could prove somewhat conservative, in the $1.60-2.00 range.

ARITHMETIC at $4.26:
- Upside +123%, downside -62%, about 2.0 to 1.
- Market-implied win probability: (4.26 - 1.60) / (9.50 - 1.60) = 33.7%.
- At my 40%: expected value 1.60 + 0.40 x 7.90 = $4.76, or +11.6%.
- At 38%: $4.60, or +8%. At 34%: zero.
- The board's +28.9% does not reproduce.

TAKEOUT LENS: comps are Biogen/Apellis (announced 31 March 2026, $41 per share cash plus a contingent value right, about $5.6B, Syfovre approved with $587M of 2025 sales) and Astellas/Iveric Bio (May 2023, about $5.9B, near approval). Plausible acquirers are Astellas and Biogen, though both now own a competing complement inhibitor, which narrows the field. I applied no lift to the target: Annexon will not have pivotal data in hand in the window, only a masked committee verdict. Takeout is undated optionality after the Q1 2027 data.

DRIVER: FDA_clinical_readout confirmed. The event is idiosyncratic and resolves on the committee's verdict, not the tape.
